column3: NKJV has “his own sheep,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “all his own.”
Close to the Greek; “allegory” is rendered “illustration.”
NKJV has “catches the sheep,” following the Textus Receptus, which repeats “the sheep”; the critical text reads “snatches them.”
NKJV begins with “The hireling flees,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text begins “because he is a hireling.”
NKJV has “am known by My own,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “My own know Me.”
NKJV has “My Father,” where the Greek has “the Father.”
Close to the Greek; “authority” is rendered “power.”
NKJV has “Now it was,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “It was then.”
Close to the Greek; “hold our soul in suspense” is rendered “keep us in doubt.”
NKJV includes “as I said to you,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV has “My Father, who has given them to Me, is greater than all,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “What My Father has given Me is greater than all.”
NKJV has “My Father”; the Greek reads “the Father.”
